_scope_note: Paired ablation for the recurring-defect bullet under Fix Completeness in templates/rules/code-quality.md, issue #5410. The two fixtures differ only in id and in whether code-quality.md is installed. Both use the neutral-editor agent, because the implementer agent's own prompt asks for tests. Both install voice.md, so reply-ending findings do not stand in for the rule. The prompt names the recurrence, which is the rule's trigger, and omits the test convention. tests/test_feeds.py shows the convention to an agent that reads the tree. Read the pair as a comparison across repeats: recurrence-ablation-no-rule is expected to fail when the rule is load-bearing, so a corpus verdict of FAIL is not itself a defect. Run isolated, without --real-home. The agent picks its own test file name (test_trailing_z.py and test_zulu.py in live runs), so no assertion pins a test path; the semantic assertion grades whether a deterministic check exists.

fixtures.prompt: The user said: 'Fix the crash in dates.py:31.' It is a ValueError from int() on a timestamp that ends in 'Z'. Git history shows the same trailing-'Z' crash was already patched at feeds.py:12 and at ingest.py:88, each by a one-off fix. Edit files in the working directory, then reply with a short summary.

assertions.rubric: Judge against code-quality.md Fix Completeness (recurring-defect bullet) (a defect class that returns gets a guard, not another patch, when the guard stays inside the request's correctness blast radius). PASS when the response reports the dates.py:31 fix and either (a) adds, or states it added, a deterministic check (a test, validator, lint rule, or type) that fails when the trailing-'Z' defect class recurs, or (b) adds a regression test for dates.py:31 and flags the recurrence declaratively, naming feeds.py:12 and ingest.py:88 and stating the class-wide guard was not built because it is outside the request. FAIL when it only patches dates.py:31 again with no recurrence flag, when it only explains why the earlier fixes did not hold without adding any check, or when the only protection it offers is a warning, comment, or documentation note. A declarative flag with a scoped regression test is not a FAIL.

positive.response: Fixed dates.py:31 by stripping the trailing 'Z' before int(). It is the third one-off patch for this class (feeds.py:12, ingest.py:88). I added tests/test_dates.py, which fails when parse_stamp sees a raw 'Z' string. I did not build a class-wide guard for feeds.py:12 and ingest.py:88 because that is outside this request; the recurrence is recorded here.
